provenance.sign_convention: not applicable: group-level data transcribed from the paper
provenance.builder: builder C (paper tables and independent oracles); transcription script kept outside the repository

source.reference: B. Antieau, A. Krause, T. Nikolaus, On the K-theory of Z/p^n (full paper PDF)
source.file: Background/Antieau, et. al. - K-Theory of Zpn.pdf

provenance.method: Appendix A cells were extracted with PyMuPDF word boxes; each cell was assigned to its column by the right edge of its bounding box (the columns are right-aligned), so blank cells (zero groups, dropped by plain text extraction) are recovered by position. Every table was then checked visually against a 3x rendering of the page, compared with an independent transcription (K1-K16, 298 cells, 0 differences), and checked against the order identity below. Figure 1 was read from the PDF words and a rendering of the page.
provenance.self_test: For every (p,n) and weight i >= 2 with both K_{2i-1} and K_{2i-2} present: sum(exponents K_{2i-1}) - sum(exponents K_{2i-2}) == i*(n-1); for i = 1, sum(exponents K_1) == n-1. All rows pass (run by a standalone Julia script at generation time).
cross_checks: Figure 1 p-parts for Z/4 and Z/8 (K1..K10, K1(Z/8) corrected) equal Appendix A.1 columns n = 2, 3.
Figure 1 p-parts for F2[z]/z^3 equal the Hesselholt-Madsen formula (test/oracles/hesselholt_madsen.jl) for (p,f,n) = (2,1,3); prime-to-p parts are 2^i - 1 in degree 2i-1.
Example 1.7 (printed p. 4): |K_r(Z/4)| 2-parts 2, 2, 8, then 2^i in degree 2i-1 (i >= 3) and 0 in even degrees >= 4, for all printed rows K1..K59.
Angeltveit range: K_{2i-1}(Z/p^n) = [i(n-1)] (cyclic) for 1 <= i <= p-2, K_{2i-2} = 0 for 2 <= i <= p-1, and K_{2p-2} = [1], for every printed column.

conventions.appendix_A: exponents: sorted list [a_1,...] meaning K_r(Z/p^n; Z_p) = sum_j Z/p^{a_j}; [] means the group is zero (blank cell in the paper). Cells marked 'x' (not computed within 48 h) are omitted from appendix_A and listed in provenance.appendix_A_not_computed. K_{2i-1} = H^1(Z_p(i)) and K_{2i-2} = H^2(Z_p(i)) for i >= 2.
conventions.figure_1: integral K-groups K_r(R), r = 1..10, for R in {F2, Z/4, Z/8, F2[z]/z^3} (all with residue field F_2, p = 2). 'group' is the integral group (corrected where noted), 'p_exponents' its 2-primary part as a sorted exponent list, 'prime_to_p_order' the order of its odd part as a decimal string (= 2^i - 1 for r = 2i-1, '1' for even r).
